sentences.text: Technosaurus is an extinct genus of silesaurid dinosauriforms named after Texas Tech University. The genus was established by Sankar Chatterjee in 1984, with the type species designated as T. smalli.
The original description relied on specimen TTUP P9021, which included a premaxilla, two lower jaw pieces, a vertebra, and an astragalus.
Technosaurus belongs to the family Silesauridae.
It is classified within the infraclass Archosauromorpha and placed in the unranked order Ornithodira.
The parent group of Technosaurus is Sulcimentisauria.
Technosaurus lived during the Late Triassic, specifically the Norian stage, between 227.3 and 205.7 million years ago.
Fossils were found in the Cooper Canyon Formation and the Bull Canyon Formation, both located in Texas, United States.

Irmis et al. (2007) found no unambiguously dinosaurian characteristics in the skull fragments of Technosaurus. Later studies concluded that Technosaurus is a valid genus but cannot be definitively classified beyond Archosauriformes incertae sedis.
